issue: Collocation slightly off: 'lebih berat dari batas dua puluh kilo' compares weight to a limit word-for-word from English ('heavier than the limit'). Check-in agents say the bag 'melebihi batas' (exceeds the limit) or 'kelebihan X kilo'.

fix.target: Maaf, bagasi Anda melebihi batas dua puluh kilo.
fix.english: Sorry, your luggage is over the twenty-kilo limit.
fix.grammar: melebihi = to go over: melebihi batas dua puluh kilo = over the twenty-kilo limit.

issue: English calque: 'bayar untuk bagasi tambahan' copies 'pay FOR'. Indonesian bayar takes the thing paid directly: 'bayar bagasi tambahan' or 'bayar biaya bagasi tambahan'.

fix.target: Saya mau bayar biaya bagasi tambahan ini.
fix.english: I want to pay the fee for this extra luggage.

issue: 'jadwal baru keluar satu jam lagi' is ambiguous for a learner: 'baru' reads either as adjective (new schedule) or as the adverb 'only then' (the schedule only comes out in an hour). A definiteness marker on 'baru' removes the trap.

fix.target: Kata petugas, jadwal barunya keluar satu jam lagi.
fix.english: According to the officer, the new schedule comes out in an hour.

issue: Register: 'tersumbat' is the written/technical word for clogged; a guest complaining at the front desk says 'mampet'. Q3 hotel-complaint dialogue should model the spoken word (policy rule 2 direction).

fix.target: Toilet di kamar kami mampet sejak siang tadi.
fix.english: The toilet in our room has been clogged since midday.
fix.grammar: mampet = clogged, the everyday word; tersumbat is what a plumber's report says.

issue: Ungrammatical verb+adjective string: 'air ... keluar kecil sekali' (the water comes-out small). Natural phrasing nominalizes the coming-out: 'keluarnya kecil' or simply 'airnya kecil sekali' for weak pressure.

fix.target: Air di kamar mandi keluarnya kecil sekali pagi ini.
fix.english: The water in the bathroom is only coming out in a trickle this morning.
fix.grammar: keluarnya kecil = its flow is weak: -nya turns keluar (come out) into 'the coming-out'.

issue: Tip misparses the sentence: in 'masalah air panasnya', -nya attaches to the whole noun phrase 'masalah air panas' (the hot-water problem we mentioned), not to 'air panas' alone. Glossing it as 'its hot water (the hotel's)' teaches the wrong bracketing. Sentence itself is fine.

fix.target: Masalah air panasnya selesai setelah teknisi datang.
fix.english: The hot water problem was resolved after the technician came.
fix.grammar: -nya on a whole phrase marks it as the one already discussed: masalah air panasnya = that hot-water problem.

issue: Meaning error: 'semua keluarga' = 'all the families', not 'the whole family'. For one family fitting in the car it must be 'seluruh keluarga', 'sekeluarga', or 'semua anggota keluarga'. Gloss and target diverge.

fix.target: Ayah menyewa mobil besar supaya seluruh keluarga muat.
fix.english: Dad rented a big car so the whole family would fit.
fix.grammar: seluruh = the whole of one thing: seluruh keluarga = the whole family; semua keluarga = all the (separate) families.

issue: Translationese: 'buat permohonan' calques 'make a wish' with a bureaucratic noun — permohonan is a formal application (visa, permit). At a birthday people say 'make a wish' in English or 'ucapkan harapan/permohonanmu dalam hati'.

fix.target: Ayo tiup lilinnya, jangan lupa ucapkan harapanmu dulu!
fix.english: Come on, blow out the candles — don't forget to make your wish first!
fix.grammar: harapan = a hope/wish, from harap: ucapkan harapanmu = say your wish.

issue: Grammar/gloss mismatch: 'ulang tahun kembar mereka' reads as 'their twin birthday' — kembar is an adjective. 'Their twins' needs a head noun: 'anak kembar mereka' or 'si kembar'.

fix.target: Kami merayakan ulang tahun anak kembar mereka di taman kota.
fix.english: We celebrated their twins' birthday at the city park.

issue: Doubled beneficiary: membawakan already means 'bring FOR someone', so 'membawakan mainan untuk keponakan' marks the beneficiary twice. Either 'membawakan keponakan mainan' or plain 'membawa mainan untuk keponakan'.

fix.target: Selain kue, kami juga membawakan keponakan mainan.
fix.english: Besides cakes, we also brought our nephews and nieces toys.
fix.grammar: membawakan puts the person right after the verb: membawakan keponakan mainan = brought the nieces and nephews toys.

issue: Spelling: Indonesian standard is 'Sumatera' (KBBI/official); 'Sumatra' is the English spelling. Target-language text should model the Indonesian form.

fix.target: Tahun ini keluarga dari Sumatera juga ikut datang.
fix.english: This year the family from Sumatra is coming along too.
